title: LRU cache in Java
idea: An LRU cache pairs a key-to-node HashMap with a doubly linked list in use order, so get, put and evict all run in O(1) average time.

analogy.text: Receipts on a spike: a receipt you use goes back on top, and when the spike is full the bottom one is thrown away.
analogy.breaks: Finding a receipt mid-spike is slow; the map finds a node instantly.

points: The map finds a key's node directly, without walking the list.
Every hit or replace unlinks the node and relinks it at the head.
Sentinel head and tail nodes remove every null check from linking.
When full, the node just before the tail sentinel is the LRU victim.

steps.caption: Three puts fill the cache. Each new node is linked right after the head.
`get` on tea finds its node in the map and moves it to the front.
Putting soda into a full cache unlinks the node before the tail: coffee.
Putting juice again replaces its value and moves it to the front. Nothing is evicted.
`remove` deletes tea from the map and unlinks its node.
A later `get` on coffee misses: the map no longer has the key.

code.title: Map plus linked list
code.caption: The hand-built version interviewers ask for. It fuses store and LRU order in one class; `BoundedCache` keeps the pluggable route.

walk.text: Fill a three-entry cache, then print the list after each step.
A node keeps its key, so eviction can also delete it from the map.
The map indexes nodes; two sentinels mark the newest and oldest ends.
A hit moves the node to the front. A miss changes nothing.
Replacing a key updates the value and refreshes it; no eviction.
Full: unlink the node before the tail and drop its key from the map.
Four pointer writes link a node; two unlink it. All O(1).

code.title: LinkedHashMap shortcut
code.caption: The same trace with the JDK's access-ordered map. It prints keys oldest first.

walk.text: Replay the exact operations of the hand-built version.
The third constructor argument true switches to access order.
After each put of a new key the map asks whether to drop its eldest entry.

pitfalls: Forgetting to store the key in the node leaves evicted keys in the map.
A replace must move the node too, or a fresh value is evicted first.
In an interview, offer `LinkedHashMap` first, then build the list if asked.

quiz.q: What does the line starting with put soda print?
quiz.why: The get made tea most recent, so coffee sat just before the tail. Soda evicts coffee and goes to the front.

takeaway: Map for lookup, linked list for order: every LRU step is O(1).

starters: Why a doubly linked list and not a singly linked one?
How does LinkedHashMap keep access order internally?
What would change to evict by total bytes instead of count?
